status: pilot wording; not a validated psychometric scale

items.label: Which best describes your current role?
How many years of paid software development experience do you have?
How familiar are you with JavaScript or Node.js programming?
How familiar are you with writing SQL queries?
How familiar are you with file paths and file-reading APIs?
Have you completed formal secure-coding training?
options: multiple courses or substantial work training

items.label: In the last month, how often did you use a coding agent that can edit files?
Before today, how often had you used Antigravity agent mode?
When you use agent-generated code, how often do you inspect its changed lines before keeping it?
A program builds SQL by inserting a request value directly inside a quoted WHERE clause. Could some request value change which rows the query returns?
A program joins a user-supplied file name to an allowed folder before reading the file, with no further check. Could some name make it read outside that folder?

checkpoint.title: Review this exact proposed change
checkpoint.timing: after confirmed candidate exposure; before editing the frozen proposal

items.label: Will you provisionally keep or reject this proposed change?
For this exact proposed code, what is the chance (0–100%) that it meets the security requirement shown above?
What evidence led to that estimate?
What, if anything, will you check before final submission?
During this task, how often did you know your next implementation step before asking the agent?
How often did you use the agent to compare possible approaches or learn an unfamiliar API?
How familiar did this task feel before you began?
How difficult was this task for you?
How much time pressure did you feel?
Overall, how much did you rely on the agent's changes in this task?
Which part felt like carrying out a known plan, and which part felt like finding an approach?
Did anything learned in the first task affect how you approached the second? If so, what?
Did your way of reviewing agent changes change between tasks? If so, how?
Across these tasks, how willing were you to rely on the agent's code without an additional security check?
Is there anything important about your decisions or the tool that we should ask about in the interview?
